sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in SeaTac?
sections.html:
SeaTac is a small, fast-growing city south of Seattle, and its borders wrap around the region's main airport. The Census Bureau estimates 34,578 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 10.0 percent from the 2020 base. The city covers about 10 square miles of land and incorporated on February 28, 1990. Its name comes from the nickname of Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

Older neighborhoods within the city include Angle Lake, Bow Lake, McMicken Heights and Riverton Heights, all of which existed before incorporation. Owner-occupied homes are a minority here, and the typical value sits well below Seattle's. This table compares SeaTac with the country, using Census Bureau figures for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

sections.h2: How does the airport affect a SeaTac house sale?
sections.html:
The airport affects almost every parcel in the city, and buyers know it. Seattle-Tacoma International Airport was dedicated on October 31, 1944, and it covers roughly three square miles inside city limits. The Port of Seattle owns and runs it, and the city's boundaries wrap around it.

Noise complaints in the 1960s and 1970s led the Port and King County to the Sea-Tac Communities Plan of 1976. It was the first program in the country where an airport operator bought homes and school buildings next to the airport and soundproofed others. About 420 acres of vacated land north of the airport became North SeaTac Park, which now has fields, trails and a community center.

The climate adds a second layer. The airport weather station averages 39.34 inches of precipitation a year across about 156 days, with most of it from October through March, and about 6.3 inches of snow. The state disclosure form asks whether the roof has leaked in the last five years, so fix or disclose any old leak before you list.

sections.h2: What brings buyers and renters to SeaTac?
sections.html:
Jobs and transit. Alaska Airlines and Horizon Air are headquartered in SeaTac, and the city reports more than 900 businesses with nearly 40,000 employees, including close to 80 Fortune 1000 companies. Federal facilities in the city include the Federal Detention Center and an NTSB field office. The mean commute for residents is 25.4 minutes.

These are the transit and road links in the city:

  • Link light rail stops at SeaTac/Airport station and Angle Lake station.
  • King County Metro runs the RapidRide A Line on International Boulevard (State Route 99) and the RapidRide F Line on Southcenter Boulevard.
  • State Route 518 and the Airport Expressway connect the city to the freeway system, and parts of Interstate 5 and State Route 509 fall within city limits.
  • Some Sound Transit Express buses terminate at the airport and nearby hubs.

sections.h2: Which schools serve a SeaTac address?
sections.html:
Highline Public Schools serves most of the city. Elementary schools for the Highline portion include Bow Lake, Madrona and McMicken Heights in SeaTac, plus Cedarhurst in Burien. Most residents are zoned to Chinook Middle School and Tyee High School, while some go to Sylvester Middle School and Highline High School in Burien. Residents north of the airport are generally zoned to Glacier Middle School and then Highline High School.

Small parts of SeaTac are in the Kent School District and the Renton School District. If your house is near a boundary, check the district for the correct school assignment before you give buyers an answer. The King County Library System runs the Valley View Library in the city, and the city operates seven parks, including Angle Lake Park, North SeaTac Park, Valley Ridge Park and the Grandview Park off-leash area.

sections.h2: What rules apply if my SeaTac house is a rental?
sections.html:
You need a business license to operate a rental unit in SeaTac, and the city sends you to the Washington Department of Revenue to apply online. Landlords must also give each tenant the city's Renting in SeaTac Guide, which explains tenant and landlord rights, evictions, deposits, repairs and notices. The city's landlord page lists legal help, tenant protections and rebates for energy upgrades at some multifamily buildings.

If you want to sell a single-family rental and the tenant must leave first, RCW 59.18.650 sets a 90 day written notice period. The owner has to try to sell within 30 days after the tenant moves out, usually by listing the house at a reasonable price or advertising it on the multiple listing service. If the owner relists it for rent or takes it off the market within 90 days, the law presumes the owner never meant to sell. A tenant removed in violation of the section can recover the greater of actual damages or three times the monthly rent, plus fees and costs.

Ask the city of SeaTac whether any code complaint or open permit is attached to the address before you list.

sections.h2: What does closing cost a seller in SeaTac?
sections.html:
The main item is Washington's real estate excise tax, which sellers normally pay. If the seller does not pay, the buyer is responsible and the unpaid tax can attach to the property as a lien. The state portion is 1.1 percent on the part of the price up to $525,000 and 1.28 percent on the next slice up to $1,525,000. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the first break moves to $551,000. At the $519,700 Census median value, the state portion would be about $5,717 before the local rate, which King County adds.

The tax is due to the county treasurer when the sale happens, and the Department of Revenue treats the notarization date of the deed as the date of sale. Late payment accrues interest. Ask the King County treasurer for the SeaTac local rate and for your property tax balance, and ask your escrow officer how the current year's tax will be split between you and the buyer.

You will also sign the state's seller disclosure statement. It must reach the buyer within five business days after the contract is accepted, and the buyer then has three business days to rescind. The form asks about easements, shared driveways, sewer connections, wood stoves, drainage, and whether the property has any shorelines, wetlands, floodplains or critical areas.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale worth considering in SeaTac?
sections.html:
It can be, especially if the house needs work, is occupied by a tenant, or has title or tax problems that would stall a financed buyer. Compare offers against what a listing would net after repairs, the excise tax and carrying costs, and keep a few points in mind:

  • Ask for the closing date and who pays escrow and title charges in writing.
  • Gather any permits and receipts for additions or major repairs.
  • Tell the buyer about tenants and the lease term before an offer is signed.

You can request a cash offer for your SeaTac house and weigh it against a listing estimate.

faqs.q: How many people live in SeaTac, Washington?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 34,578 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is up from 31,454 counted in the 2020 census. About 46.5 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to rent out a house in SeaTac?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a business license to operate a rental unit and directs landlords to the Washington Department of Revenue to apply online. Landlords must also give each tenant a copy of the city's Renting in SeaTac Guide.

faqs.q: Which school district is SeaTac in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Highline Public Schools, with most residents zoned to Chinook Middle School and Tyee High School. Small parts of the city are in the Kent and Renton school districts, so confirm the district for your address.

faqs.q: How much notice must I give a tenant if I want to sell the house?
faqs.a: At least 90 days' advance written notice for a single-family residence under RCW 59.18.650. You must then list the house or advertise it for sale at a reasonable price within 30 days after the tenant leaves, or the law presumes you did not intend to sell.

faqs.q: What is the state excise tax on a SeaTac sale?
faqs.a: The state portion is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 of the price, 1.28 percent up to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent up to $3,025,000 and 3 percent above that, with a local rate added. The break points change for sales beginning January 1, 2027.
